title: Optimising total RNA quality and quantity by phenol-chloroform extraction method from human visceral adipose tissue: A standardisation study
author: Roy, Tomo, et al.
materials: 4. Carefully remove the fat layer by pipetting.

steps.title: Prepare equipment and workspace
steps.instruction: Autoclave all glassware and surgical instruments (scalpel, scissors, forceps); pre‑identify and label microcentrifuge tubes; immediately submerge freshly excised abdominal VAT samples in sterile containers containing 1 % PBS and transport to the laboratory; set the centrifuge temperature to 4 °C; clean the bench with 70 % ethanol or another suitable decontaminant.

steps.title: Wash and weigh tissue
steps.instruction: Wash the fresh tissue samples with 1 % PBS solution, then weigh the tissue on an analytical balance, using no more than 500 mg of VAT; if less tissue is available, adjust the TRIzol volume proportionally.

steps.title: Dissect, mince and homogenise
steps.instruction: Dissect the samples to obtain pure adipose tissue, mince into fine pieces, and place the minced tissue in a 2 mL tube (use a 1.5 mL tube for <500 mg tissue). Homogenise with a Teflon homogenizer (GenetixBiotech) at 3000 rpm in a discontinuous manner, allowing 5–10 s per stroke, keeping the tubes on ice throughout.

steps.title: Centrifuge homogenate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the homogenate at 12 000 × g for 10 min (centrifuge pre‑set to 4 °C). A visible fat layer will form on the upper surface of the aqueous phase.

steps.title: Remove fat layer
steps.instruction: Carefully pipette off the fat layer. Do not transfer the aqueous supernatant to a new tube, because with ≤250 µL TRIzol (the reduced volume used in this optimisation) separating the supernatant reduces RNA yield and is impractical.
